f4b4bb981e:163b065d3b29a229.title: Vexto - Incident Response Desktop App UI UX
f4b4bb981e:163b065d3b29a229.summary: Vexto is a desktop app that gives our dispatch team real-time visibility into every vehicle in the fleet. It brings live GPS tracking, accident detection, and webcam verification into one system, so we can confirm incidents faster, respond with full context, and keep the whole operation under control. The project moved from fleet data audit to system architecture, incident logic, and map-based UX flows. Time was spent aligning live GPS, accident detection, and webcam feeds into one platform. The deepest work was structuring real-time logic that stays reliable at scale. We prioritized map-first navigation over list-based menus, since dispatchers think in location, not records. Analysis showed incident context mattered more than raw data, so we surfaced vehicle status, connectivity, and live webcam access in one card ? cutting verification time and improving response control.

f4b4bb981e:45ba4d56110252b6.title: Global Digital Collaboration Conference
f4b4bb981e:45ba4d56110252b6.summary: Visual identity for the Global Digital Collaboration Conference 2026 in Geneva. GDC brings together governments, international organisations, technology companies and other stakeholders to collaborate on the digital infrastructure and standards that increasingly connect our world. At the heart of the identity is the Global Barcode, an idea conceived by GDC founder Daniel Goldscheider. It translates the flags of all UN member states into simple vertical colour codes, based on the colours and their proportions within each national flag. Put together, they form one global code. And one very, very long flag. This became the starting point for the visual identity: an endless flag that folds, bends and winds its way through posters, spaces, shirts, lanyards and the conference itself. For the participant badges, the principle became personal: each name generates its own individual colour code.

f4b4bb981e:eaf91ce84cda68fb.title: Bradesco - São João
f4b4bb981e:eaf91ce84cda68fb.summary: We were invited by Lovely to create this São João campaign for Bradesco, inspired by the friendly rivalry between Caruaru and Campina Grande, home to two of Brazil's biggest June festivals. Building on the campaign concept, we developed a visual language inspired by Northeastern Brazilian folk culture and the tradition of repente, a form of improvised poetic dueling built around rhymes, wit, and playful provocation. We created a series of handcrafted illustrations that bring these two cities together, exploring the colors, shapes, and visual elements associated with São João celebrations. Each composition was designed to capture the spirit of rivalry while also celebrating a sense of unity. The result is a series of pieces that turn rivalry into connection and visually express the campaign's central message: the greatest São João is the one we create together.

f4b4bb981e:ec58b8cd447803b8.title: FoundersCard
f4b4bb981e:ec58b8cd447803b8.summary: FoundersCard has built a unique proposition around access?connecting an ambitious community of entrepreneurs and business leaders with exceptional benefits, experiences, and opportunities. Our challenge was to create a digital experience that felt as considered and valuable as the membership itself. We began by rethinking the experience from the ground up. Stripping away complexity, sharpening the hierarchy, and creating a clearer way to communicate the breadth of the FoundersCard world. The goal was simple: make something premium without feeling exclusive for the sake of it, and sophisticated without becoming complicated. A new visual language brought that thinking to life. Bold typography, confident layouts, elevated imagery, and a more editorial approach gave the brand greater presence and personality. A flexible design system created consistency across the experience while leaving room for partners, benefits, destinations, and stories to each have their own moment.

It was the Barryvox—an avalanche beacon used to search for victims buried in the snow. For Fujiwara, who has carried one into the backcountry for years, it is quite literally a lifesaver.Almost three years later, the new Barryvox S2 FRGMT Edition takes the upgraded Barryvox S2 and coats it in fragment's signature blue and white. It features a special "FRGMT x MAMMUT" logo and a custom startup animation. The core functionality, however, remains untouched—a deliberate choice to leave perfected safety equipment exactly as it is.“To me, it doesn't feel like a second time, but more like a natural extension,” says Fujiwara. What did he add to the new model, and what did he leave alone? And with the environment surrounding snow mountains in flux, how is he approaching the snow himself these days? We caught up with him to follow up on our interview from three years ago.Hypebeast: It's been about three years since your last collaboration with MAMMUT. Can you tell us how you came to make another Barryvox?Hiroshi Fujiwara: To me, it doesn't really feel like a second time; it's more like a natural extension. That said, the theme this time is that there's a new Barryvox out. I'm the type who always wants to upgrade my beacon to the latest model, so it felt like the perfect invitation at the perfect time.This time, it's based on the new Barryvox S2.Apparently it's lighter, thinner, and supports voice assistance. I haven't actually used it myself yet, though.How did you approach the design?Like last time, changing the color is about all we can do. It's designed for pure functionality, so it's not the kind of life-or-death equipment you should be messing around with. Within those limits, I did what I could.Is there a specific kind of fun in designing a product with such limited touchpoints?It's less…

a4977d3fa4:b41d2d9f5ca4bf6d.title: Puma's 'Slipcat' Transforms into a Boot Silhouette for Fall and Winter
a4977d3fa4:b41d2d9f5ca4bf6d.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b41d2d9f5ca4bf6d.summary: Puma is introducing a new silhouette for the Fall/Winter 2026 season: the 'Slipcat Boots.'The Slipcat is a model born from Puma's motorsport heritage. According to Puma, the original Slipcat was created by combining the base of the brand's archive racing shoe, the Future Cat, with a slip-on silhouette. It features a low, sleek shape and a low-profile outsole inspired by racing shoes.The newly revealed Slipcat Boots expand on this design for the fall and winter seasons. While maintaining the low-profile silhouette of the original model, soft suede and fleece details have been added for a more seasonal look.The most eye-catching feature is the heightened shaft. You can wear the shaft fully extended as a boot or fold it down to reveal the fleece detail, allowing you to style it into different silhouettes depending on your preference. It essentially combines the sleek design of a racing shoe with the details of a boot in one model.The Slipcat Boots, a fresh variation of Puma's racing archive, will be released on October 1st. More information about the product can be found on Puma Korea's official online store and Instagram. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:b69a618fb0f05536.title: How to Style KEEN's Jasper Merko — Hairstylist Kazuma Baba's Take
a4977d3fa4:b69a618fb0f05536.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b69a618fb0f05536.summary: The Jasper Merko takes KEEN's classic Jasper—a hybrid of a climbing shoe and a comfort shoe—and refines it into a more minimalist, lightweight silhouette. Inspired by contour lines, the low-profile sole lends the foot a unique presence while delivering a nearly barefoot sensation. A classic upper paired with a modern sole: this quiet contrast defines the distinct personality of the shoe.Following our previous installment, this time we feature Kazuma Baba, owner of the hair salon STILL LIGHTS. He styled the Jasper Merko by bridging his running background with his everyday wardrobe. Baba, who was originally drawn to the shoe's minimalist aesthetic, paired this outdoor-rooted yet distinctly fashion-forward design with a long-sleeve tee from the running wear brand SATISFY.As someone who has been running for 14 or 15 years, the line between sports and fashion is incredibly blurred for him. Slipping into the Jasper Merko, he immediately noticed its ground-hugging low center of gravity and a fit that naturally molds to the foot. The simple feeling of it being "light and thin" was a massive draw for someone who typically steers clear of bulky footwear.When putting the look together, after experimenting with sweatpants, he ultimately settled on a sleek pair of slacks. By deliberately grounding the shoe's sporty elements with a highly fashionable piece, he unlocked a new side of the Jasper Merko. Rather than remaining confined to an outdoor or athletic context, it effortlessly slots into a fashion lover's everyday wardrobe. It blends seamlessly into the rhythm of the city, transcending age and gender. That incredible versatility is precisely what makes this pair so appealing.The Jasper Merko is currently available at the KEEN official online store and at KEEN retail locations. a4977d3fa4:1eaa3d2aa9b60977.title: New York Giants Have Waived Odell Beckham Jr.
a4977d3fa4:1eaa3d2aa9b60977.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:1eaa3d2aa9b60977.summary: Summary The New York Giants have waived veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr after a brief three-game reunionBeckham logged 19 snaps and zero receptions before being released to make room for punt returner Braxton BerriosThe three-time Pro Bowler is not currently expected to join the team's practice squad The New York Giants have officially released wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. following a brief second stint with the organization. The 33-year-old fan favorite departs the franchise without recording a single catch across the opening weeks of the season.Beckham's roster spot became vulnerable as New York needed to convert punt returner Braxton Berrios to the 53-man roster after exhausting his practice squad elevations. To address additional depth following outside linebacker Brian Burns' season-ending ACL injury, the Giants also signed wide receiver Charlie Jones.During his return to Big Blue, Beckham logged 19 offensive snaps across three games and was targeted just once—a pass from quarterback Jameis Winston during Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans. Despite earning a spot on the initial 53-man roster as the fifth receiver out of training camp, the veteran saw limited opportunity. Sources indicate that Beckham is not expected to be added to the Giants' practice squad, concluding his second chapter in East Rutherford. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:58ab7f7affadb4a3.title: Liev Schreiber and Zazie Beetz Hunt a Serial Killer in Apple TV's 'Nocturne' Trailer
a4977d3fa4:58ab7f7affadb4a3.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:58ab7f7affadb4a3.summary: Summary Apple TV has released the official trailer and key art for its upcoming crime drama series 'Nocturne'The 10-episode series stars Liev Schreiber Zazie Beetz and Stephen Graham and is adapted from Lars Kepler's bestselling novelsThe psychological thriller debuts globally on October 30, 2026 with a two-episode premiere Apple TV has unveiled the official trailer for Nocturne, a gripping 10-episode crime drama series starring Liev Schreiber, Zazie Beetz, and Stephen Graham. Adapted from Lars Kepler’s internationally bestselling Joona Linna novel series, the psychological thriller is created for television by BAFTA Award winner Rowan Joffé and co-showrun alongside John Hlavin.The narrative centers on Jonah Lynn (Schreiber), an ex-soldier turned homicide detective who leaves behind the rough streets of Philadelphia for a quieter life in a small Western Pennsylvania town. His search for peace is disrupted when a cunning serial killer named Jurek Walter (Graham) targets the local community and Lynn's family. In a desperate effort to locate Walter's final missing victim, Lynn sends his surrogate daughter, FBI Agent Saga Bauer (Beetz), into a high-stakes showdown against the killer.The series features an ensemble cast including Bill Camp, Rory Culkin, Chrissy Metz, Poorna Jagannathan, and Gary Carr. Directed in its opening episodes by Emmy Award winner Tim Van Patten, the project is produced by A+E Studios in association with Range Studios, with Schreiber, Beetz, Joffé, Hlavin, and author duo Lars Kepler (Alexandra Coelho Ahndoril and Alexander Ahndoril) serving as executive producers.Nocturne premieres globally on Friday, October 30, 2026, on Apple TV with its first two episodes, followed by weekly releases every Friday through December 25. Read more at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:88d7596d6208180d.title: Al Diaz on the Real Meaning Behind SAMO With Basquiat
a4977d3fa4:88d7596d6208180d.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:88d7596d6208180d.summary: For Al Diaz, the history of SAMO© has never been as simple as the story that followed it. Created with Jean-Michel Basquiat in the late 1970s, SAMO© has since been folded into the mythology surrounding Basquiat, often described as an alias, a conventional graffiti tag or shorthand for “Same Old Shit.” Diaz sees it differently. What the two teenagers developed was closer to an invented product: a series of cryptic, satirical messages written for anyone walking the streets of downtown New York, not just other graffiti writers.Nearly five decades later, Diaz is still pushing back against the simplified version of that history. “I’m not going to stand around and listen to a history that you’re part of being told incorrectly,” he says. “I’m not one to sit there quietly.”That conversation carries into ‘SAMO: TRANSATLANTICATION,’ Diaz’s first solo exhibition in London, which opened September 25 at D’Stassi Art. Alongside new SAMO© canvases, the exhibition presents works from his ongoing subway-signage series and mixed-media practice, offering a broader picture of an artist whose relationship with language has continued to evolve well beyond the project he created as a teenager.We spoke with Diaz about the real origins of SAMO©, working with Basquiat before the mythology took over, why “Same Old Shit” misses the point, and what it means to revisit that history nearly 50 years later.How did this exhibition come about, and what’s your relationship with the gallery?I think I met one of the guys from the gallery, Michael Howes, maybe in 2019 or ’20, about six years ago. And we did a collaboration with an artist that we were representing.And then after that, we ran an edition of two images of prints. And we did that, and then we stayed in touch over the last few years. And they’d been talking about doing a show primarily focusing on the SAMO stuff, which is something I did with Basquiat back in 1978.You revived SAMO in 2016. What made you return to it after so many years?The…

a4977d3fa4:cc9d2aa0914aa247.title: Rare David Hockney Dog Painting Goes for $3 Million USD at Christie's
a4977d3fa4:cc9d2aa0914aa247.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:cc9d2aa0914aa247.summary: Summary David Hockneys' 1995 work "Dog Painting 17" will be auctioned at Christie's London on October 14The painting, which depicts his first dachshund, Stanley, curled up on a bed, is just one of six works from the artist's "Dog Series" believed to be in private hands Just as iconic as David Hockney’s draw to Californian pools or the rolling hills of Yorkshire, as real Hockney heads know, was his love for his dogs, Stanley and Boodgie. The dachshunds starred in his painted “Dog Series," created between 1994 and 1995. And for the first time, one of them is hitting the auction block.“Dog Painting 17” (1995) heads to Christie’s London on October 14, carrying an estimate of £1.5 million to £2.5 million GBP ($1.99 million to $3.3 million USD). The painting figures Stanley fast asleep, curled up in a dog bed, and is only one of six from the series believed to be in private hands, according to the house, with the rest in the keeping of the David Hockney Foundation. “This is such an exciting painting for us,” said Tessa Lord, Christie’s head of postwar and contemporary art. “The rarity is kind of extraordinary.”While the piece embodies the spontaneity and textural fluidity of Hockney’s brushwork, “Dog Painting 17” also highlights an important chapter for the late British legend. It was created during a time of immense grief for Hockney, having lost several friends to AIDS and one of his closest to pancreatic cancer. His dogs, and the dog paintings, provided some much-needed light in a dark period.“He felt such a loss of love, this was kind of a catharsis for him,” Lord continued. “I love the fact that there is this kind of innocence to it but it is so much more than that. There’s a universality to it … it’s so much more than just a portrait of a dog.”“Dog Painting 17” will be on view at Christie’s London galleries between October 8 and when it goes under the hammer during Frieze London. a4977d3fa4:fe8c7a437f563f40.title: Drake's 'FOMO' Will Hit Streaming Platforms on October 1st
a4977d3fa4:fe8c7a437f563f40.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:fe8c7a437f563f40.summary: Summary Drake announced during a Sept. 28 stream that most songs from his hour-long "not-so-short-film" 'FOMO' will hit streaming platforms on Thursday, Oct. 1.The film compiles Toronto summer vignettes, celebrity cameos, and new music, including unreleased collabs with Don Toliver, Yeat, and OnlyHeaven, serving as a visual prelude to his upcoming 2027 tour. While streaming this past Monday, September 28th, Drake announced that he’ll be dropping most of the tracks from his “not-so-short-film," ‘FOMO’ on Thursday, October 1st.“There’s a bunch of songs coming to streaming on Thursday, so all the songs that you guys have been asking [for], well… not all of them, but enough of them are coming on Thursday," Drake stated.Directed by Theo Skudra, Liam Macrae, Jake Schreier, Zong Li, and Glenn Michael, and described by the artist as “self-funded surrealism,” Fear of Missing Out compiled an hour's worth of Toronto summer vignettes, interspersed with music videos from his recent albums Maid of Honour, Habibti, and ICEMAN. The video included scenes on a speedboat on Lake Ontario, at the Casa Loma mansion, around the Canadian National Exhibition fair, and an Iron Man suit cameo with Loe Shimmy. Guest stars across the visual include Sexyy Red, Winnie Harlow, Stunna Sandy, Kevin Durant, Lena the Plug, and Drake’s mother, Sandi Graham.Alongside existing visuals for tracks like “WNBA,” “Road Trips,” and “Hoe Phase,” the film debuts new music including a slowed-down remix of Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” featuring Don Toliver, "Quebec" — which is out now on YouTube, and additional collaborations with Toliver, Yeat, and OnlyHeaven.The YouTube stream was set to private following its debut, returning on September 17th, with Fear of Missing Out serving as a visual prelude to Drake’s scheduled 2027 concert tour, which will mark his first North American trek since 2023. a4977d3fa4:dff7271d7702834c.title: Kader Sylla Unveils First Signature Shoe With adidas Skateboarding

a4977d3fa4:dff7271d7702834c.summary: SummaryKader Sylla’s first signature adidas shoe, the $110 "Kader," blends '90s basketball style with durable skate performance.The versatile suede sneaker launches today in two colorways, kicking off the North American leg of his global tour.Professional skater Kader Sylla has teamed up with adidas Skateboarding to introduce his first-ever signature sneaker: The Kader. I’m excited for people to experience it and take it wherever they go," he added.Drawing core inspiration from '90s adidas Equipment basketball silhouettes, the mid-top model is engineered for versatility from the streets to the skatepark. In brown suede with yellow snake stripes and black suede with purple speckled stripes, the Kader reinterprets the iconic Three Stripes by integrating them directly into the lacing system, blending branding with functional details. Built for heavy impact, the sneaker features a durable cupsole, a full-length Lightmotion midsole, Adituff underlays, and a premium suede upper.To celebrate the launch, Kader is taking his kicks on the road for a massive global World Tour. The North American leg kicks off tomorrow, October 1, bringing demos and skateshop appearances to local communities from Minneapolis to Los Angeles.Kader Sylla's adidas Skateboarding signature shoe is available now for $110 USD at adidas. a4977d3fa4:470c2e259100a654.title: InScope's Hayley Smith on What Galleries Keep Getting Wrong
a4977d3fa4:470c2e259100a654.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:470c2e259100a654.summary: Summary 'State of Art' is a new HypeArt series inviting artists, curators, collectors and other leading voices to weigh in on the ideas, debates and cultural shifts shaping contemporary art. Through intimate questions and personal recommendations, the series offers a closer look at what is exciting the art world, what needs to change and where things may be heading next. For decades, gallery representation was seen as a major sign that an artist had made it. Galleries opened doors to collectors, institutions and curators, while artists depended on them to build visibility, establish a market and grow their careers. That dynamic is starting to shift.Artists can now build global audiences, sell work directly, stage their own shows and create communities without waiting for traditional gatekeepers. But for Hayley River Smith, director of InScope (formerly Scope Art Show), that does not mean galleries are losing their relevance. It means the relationship between artists and galleries has to change.For the latest edition of Hypeart’s ‘State of Art,’ Smith talks about what meaningful representation looks like in 2026, whether the traditional 50/50 split still holds up and why belief, trust and real investment in an artist may matter more than representation alone."What people are craving now is real connection beyond what is transactional."Do artists still need galleries? Why or why not?For me the question isn't whether artists need galleries anymore rather what we want that relationship to be. We have spent a long time painstakingly applauding what is predictable. We know what a gallery is supposed to do, what an artist is supposed to do, what a fair is supposed to look like, and what success is supposed to look like. We have reached a point where we're looking at that model grimacing while we all continue to participate in the sameness of it all.Artists have more ways to build audiences and sell work directly than ever before, but that doesn't mean the relationships…

a4977d3fa4:7c89413c82170746.title: Blue Bottle’s First Jazz Album Is Made for Slow Listening
a4977d3fa4:7c89413c82170746.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7c89413c82170746.summary: Summary Blue Bottle Coffee debuts Notes in Repose , its first limited-edition jazz vinyl.It features 10 contemporary tracks interspersed with ambient cafe recordings.Limited to 1,500 copies, the release celebrates the brand's Signature Blends. Blue Bottle Coffee has unveiled Notes in Repose, its first-ever compilation album celebrating the shared language of jazz, coffee and composition. Created in celebration of its Signature Blends, the limited-edition vinyl brings together 10 contemporary jazz compositions from artists spanning nine cities across Blue Bottle’s North American and Asian cafe markets.The lineup includes Ali Shaheed Muhammad, Makaya McCraven, Jeff Parker, Angel Bat Dawid and the Kyoto Jazz Sextet, with the individual tracks woven together by ambient recordings captured inside Blue Bottle cafes. Conceived as an invitation to slow down and listen with greater intention, the project draws a parallel between musical composition and coffee blending — bringing distinct elements together while preserving their individual character to create a more balanced whole.Jazz has influenced Blue Bottle's creative approach since its inception, rooted in founder James Freeman’s background as a working clarinetist and inspired by the focused listening environments of Japanese jazz kissas. This deep-seated connection to music is already evident in the brand's bold, chocolatey Giant Steps blend, named after John Coltrane's iconic 1960 composition. Even the title Notes in Repose reflects that sensibility, framing the record as a moment of pause in which coffee, sound and physical album artwork become part of the same experience. Limited to 1,500 copies, Notes in Repose will be available beginning October 6 via Blue Bottle’s website while supplies last, while Giant Steps remains available year-round online and at Blue Bottle cafes. Positioned behind the grille, the built-in stage lights take cues from live concert rigs and move in response to the music, with three presets ranging from restrained ambience to a more pronounced light show. a4977d3fa4:8814ddfaea8dd4d6.summary: Wherever LISA travels, whether it's a stadium on another continent, a fashion week front row, or a hotel suite she'll leave by morning, one thing always comes with her. It isn't a jewel or a lucky charm. It's a pair of slippers. "I bring them everywhere with me whenever I travel and they are so cozy and make me feel more at home," she says.It's a concise explanation, and an unexpectedly tender detail from someone who spends most of her working life being looked at. The LISA most of the world knows is the one onstage: exact, electric, one of the most recognized performers in pop. But the person carrying slippers from city to city points to another LISA — the one who looks for home wherever she lands. That tension between the star and the homebody is what drives her newest project as creative director: Meta Glasses by LISA. The collection comes in two frames, each representing the two sides to her. The Adventurer, with Blush lenses, is for the LISA who takes her time. The Capri, a sharp cat-eye, is for the LISA who walks onstage.She's never pretended there's only one of her. When she stepped out on her own with her dynamic debut solo album, she gave the world five different personas. Each one was a different character, and each was her. The symbol she chose for that idea was a five-pointed star, and it came up in the very first design meetings for the glasses. Now it sits on the temple tips and the case."I don’t think you have to pick just one version of yourself, so the star became my way of saying all of them can exist at once.""The star was from my first solo album, Alter Ego. The five points represent five different characters of this album," LISA shares. "I don't think you have to pick just one version of yourself, so the star became my way of saying all of them can exist at once. Putting it on the temple tips felt right because it's small and personal. You don't see it from far away, but you know it's there."Like the hidden emblem on the glasses, the things…

a4977d3fa4:b4916dac5db20bfe.title: BOOX's Card-Sized Picco E-Reader Swaps Doomscrolling for a Chapter
a4977d3fa4:b4916dac5db20bfe.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b4916dac5db20bfe.summary: Summary BOOX has opened preorders for the Picco, its smallest eReader so far, with a 3.97-inch monochrome ePaper screen in a body weighing about 58 gramsAn included magnetic ring case lets the device attach to the back of a smartphone for a single pocket carryThe Picco is the first device in BOOX Tiles, a new category that takes ePaper beyond standard eReaders and tablets BOOX has opened preorders for the Picco, a card-sized eReader and the smallest device the ePaper specialist has made. Built around a 3.97-inch monochrome display and weighing roughly 58 grams, the Picco is meant to replace a phone during brief stretches of idle time, from the morning commute to the checkout line. It is also the first product under BOOX Tiles, a new line exploring ePaper hardware in form factors outside the brand's usual readers and tablets.Similar in size to a single playing card, the Picco slips into a pocket or small bag, and the magnetic ring case in the box lets it snap onto the back of a phone so both devices travel as one. The idea is to put the book right where the scrolling habit already lives.The screen is small but sharp, at 235 PPI, with a front light that adjusts between warm and cool tones for different lighting conditions. Navigation works two ways, through the touchscreen or with physical page-turn buttons, and four-way rotation lets readers flip the orientation to suit either hand or grip.A 16GB microSD card comes included, and the slot accepts cards up to 2TB, enough for thousands of titles. Books and documents can be loaded through the BOOX Tiles app, a web browser or a USB-C connection, and the device reads a wide range of common eBook and document formats. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth handle wireless connectivity.Software keeps the focus on reading. The Picco runs a pared-back operating system that removes the busy interfaces and constant alerts of phones and tablets, adding only a few light tools: a Pomodoro timer, a to-do list and a countdown. a4977d3fa4:fc2a68c6b758e6cd.title: Diemme x Rayon Vert Turn Deadstock Tweed Into an Alpine-Ready Grappa Verde
a4977d3fa4:fc2a68c6b758e6cd.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:fc2a68c6b758e6cd.summary: Name: Diemme x Rayon Vert Grappa VerdeColorway: Olive / Sand Tweed, Green / Blue Tweed, Grey Nylon, Maroon / Cream TweedSKU: TBCMSRP: TBCRelease Date: September 30Where to Buy: DiemmeDiemme and Rayon Vert have unveiled the Grappa Verde, a four-piece take on Diemme's Grappa silhouette designed for daily wear in the outdoors. Marking the first collaboration between the two, the shoe skips modern technical textiles in favor of wool tweeds pulled from Diemme's deadstock, drawing on the fabrics once worn by the "Alpini" in the mountains.The lineup splits into three tweed options, Olive/Sand Tweed, Green/Blue Tweed and Maroon/Cream Tweed, plus a Grey Nylon version. The tweed choice is functional as much as it is nostalgic. Its dense wool weave has served as a performance fabric for centuries, holding off wind and moisture while staying breathable, warm and durable, and it keeps its shape through long stretches in cold conditions. The design brief looks back to a time when mountain clothing earned its toughness through fiber and build quality, long before synthetic coatings took over. The Grey Nylon pair updates that idea with a modern material while aiming for the same balance of protection and comfort.The Alpini in question are Italy's elite mountain infantry, a corps formed in the 1870s to defend the country's Alpine borders. Their wool-heavy kit gives the Grappa Verde both its material logic and its muted, field-ready palette.The construction supports the upper in key areas. Italian-made suede panels reinforce high-wear zones, while the interior is lined in leather and fitted with a custom-illustrated footbed on Diemme's standard latex base. Underfoot, a hand-applied rubber rand wraps the join between upper and sole, and a Vibram HIKER outsole provides grip and stability on uneven ground. Technical lacing hardware completes the build.That mountain focus comes from home. Diemme was founded in 1992 and operates out of Asolo, where the Dolomites can be seen from the…

It first surfaced in January as the closing look of JUUN.J's Fall/Winter 2026 show at the Théâtre National de Chaillot in Paris.The capsule is organized across three categories: nine menswear styles, five womenswear styles and three accessories designed to work for both. Its structural backbone is outerwear. Leather bombers and rider jackets take JUUN.J's signature oversized proportions and build them out with heavy padding, while intricate leather patchwork breaks up each panel and adds to the gear-inspired feel.That padding is the clearest link to RSRV's source material. a4977d3fa4:8254c5b617fe0a27.title: J. Press x Barbour's Revived Burghley Keeps Its Equestrian Drip Strip and Thornproof Wax
a4977d3fa4:8254c5b617fe0a27.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:8254c5b617fe0a27.summary: Summary J. Press has partnered with Barbour to bring back the Burghley, a full-length wax jacket first designed in the 1980s for riding and country wearThe coat is cut from 6 oz thornproof waxed cotton in a slimmer silhouette that ends just above the kneeRiding-specific details, including a drip strip and rear vent, carry over from the jacket's equestrian origins J. Press and Barbour have revived the Burghley, a full-length equestrian wax jacket pulled from Barbour's archive. First developed in the 1980s for horseback riding and country use, the coat returns with its original riding features intact, now offered through the American Ivy label as long trench-style outerwear gains traction in North America.The shell is made from 6 oz thornproof waxed cotton, a dense, weatherproof fabric suited to the brambles and rain the coat was built for. The fit is slimmer than the boxy wax jackets many people associate with Barbour, and the hem stops just above the knee. That length provides trench-like coverage without getting in the way in the saddle or on foot.Several details point back to the jacket's riding roots. A drip strip, originally designed to keep a horse's sweat off the rider's clothing, runs along the interior, while a roomy rear vent allows for movement when mounted. A two-way Barbour ring-pull zip lets the wearer open the coat from the bottom, a practical feature for riding that also works when sitting down in the city.The finishing touches are classic Barbour. A corduroy collar frames the neckline and pairs with a storm flap that can be closed against wind and rain, and the inside is lined in 100% cotton in the brand's signature tartan. The jacket is offered in Navy, listed as "Navy Thornproof Classic Waxed Cotton," alongside a Sage version.The J. Press x Barbour Burghley is available now via J. Press. a4977d3fa4:6852d12c0dc9cfd6.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:6852d12c0dc9cfd6.summary: Summary LeBron James made his official Philadelphia 76ers debut at media day wearing No 23The veteran forward enters season 24 alongside teammates Joel Embiid Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen BrownJames outlined his postseason focus during the session stating he did not leave his family to lose in the second round The Philadelphia 76ers officially debuted LeBron James in team colors during NBA media day. Off the court, the veteran forward confirmed he will split his time living between New York City and Philadelphia across multiple residences as the 76ers prepare for the upcoming campaign. a4977d3fa4:be255bb90c334b75.summary: 30C Engineering's Fall/Winter 2026 collection is themed "When the Runner Stops Running." Rooted in trail running, 30C turns its focus this season to the moments of pause between strides. This attention to the body is also written into the name 30C. "3" resembles a mountain ridge or the path of the body moving forward, from muscle and bone back to breath. Movement propels us outward, but also inward. "0" represents the sun and moon, signifying Orientation—the constant recalibration of oneself between departure and return. "C" is the sequence of action: Conscious, Committed, Consistent. Together, these three elements form what 30C understands as Engineering, an internal process that begins with physical practice. Through repeated runs, the body learns how to exert and release force; what once required conscious judgment gradually becomes instinct. Knowing one's own strength also means knowing how to relax. Rest comes from an awareness of the body; strength does not always need to be on display. This season uses ultra-light materials to create bolder silhouettes, with loose-fitting tops and wide-leg trousers further amplifying the shape. The use of one-piece tailoring brings clean, continuous lines, while functional details are hidden within the structure. The runner pauses, but the clothing still moves.On the day of the release, 30C hosted the "ENGINEERED FOR THE AFTER" launch event at All by Runners in Shanghai. The event kicked off with a 5KM city run, after which participants experienced the new collection up close and continued conversations about sports and everyday wear at the AFTER PARTY. Moving forward, 30C will continue to explore bolder expressions in both athletic and everyday apparel. a4977d3fa4:4998248a3ef427d6.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:4998248a3ef427d6.summary: Summary Los Angeles-based contemporary artist Ozzie Juarez and GUESS JEANS have partnered on a limited-edition line-up featuring two jacket-and-pant-denim sets and a graphic teeThe collab is available exclusively available at GUESS JEANS Melrose in Los AngelesA curation of Juarez's artworks is also on view in the store These GUESS jeans just got an adorable upgrade thanks to Los Angeles-based Ozzie Juarez. The contemporary artist and brand have partnered on a limited-edition tee and matching set collab, available exclusively at GUESS JEANS’ Melrose outpost, printing Juarez’s cute ceramic-like animals straight onto denim.Born and raised in South Los Angeles, Juarez, who also founded TLALOC Studios, uses his practice as a way to honor the city and his community is always up for him. Artifacts and icons from across the city, as well as his own cultural heritage, make their way into paintings, sculptures, and monumental public artworks, spanning everything from patterns in ancient Mesoamerican manuscripts to contemporary car culture and spills of nostalgic cartoons.As of this past year, he’s been busy making paintings of cute animal characters housed in metallized frames, echoing the architectural vernacular of Los Angeles. The figures, which show his hard-and-soft range, are the stars of his go-around with GUESS JEANS.The collection features two denim sets, each pairing pants with a classic trucker-style jacket, plus a graphic tee. Figures like a cheery zebra, droopy-eyed dog, baby duck, coquettish deer, and bird characters are scattered across garments: down the front leg and across the back pockets on the denim, and stretching the wingspan on the back of the jacket. A full-color zebra tee rounds out the lineup.If you’ve spotted Juarez at an opening or a fair, you know he always arrives fitted, so a fashion collab comes as no surprise. Beyond the GUESS JEANS collection, his first with a major brand, a few years ago he also launched Corazón de Tierra, a jewelry line…

a4977d3fa4:1b9f36b201a75c80.title: Enter Martin Margiela's Liminal Labyrinth at Konrad Fischer Galerie
a4977d3fa4:1b9f36b201a75c80.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:1b9f36b201a75c80.summary: Summary Martin Margiela unveil his first Germany exhibition at Berlin's Konrad Fischer GalerieThe exhibition features new artworks that explore themes of privacy, intimacy, and architecture, elaborating on the artist's exploration of anonymity and the human form Before Margiela left Margiela, he was known to many as the most elusive man in fashion. Even after retiring from the industry, deciding to dedicate himself to fine art, the Belgian luminary's devotion to the incognito and fraught relationship with the public eye continued to play a paramount role in his personal practice.Take "Audience" (2026), one of the new sculptures in Martin Margiela in Berlin, his first exhibition in Germany at Konrad Fischer Galerie. 20 reclaimed cinema seats are stripped of their upholstery and replaced with cold plaster and acrylic casts. An object designed for shared viewing experiences can now only be looked at.Like his exhibition at Tokyo’s Kudan House this past spring, Margiela’s Berlin show is another artful labyrinth. Paintings, sculptures, and assemblages unfold in a maze of partitions and veils, embedding an atmosphere of intimacy straight into the architecture.Other pieces include a monumental white fur gate, boxer briefs flattened into tondos, a crown of hair overwritten with a Fibonacci spiral, and new Vortex sculptures, created from what appears to be bathroom tiling, together steeping viewers deeper into themes of privacy, absence, and human presence central to Margiela's artistry.Martin Margiela in Berlin is now on view until December 19.Konrad Fischer GalerieNeue Grünstraße 12.10179 Berlin Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:487d90a9200e2f54.title: Wrangler and imogene + willie Teamed Up to Craft the Ultimate Vintage Americana Collection
a4977d3fa4:487d90a9200e2f54.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:487d90a9200e2f54.summary: American denim history just got a fresh, carefully crafted update. Wrangler, an iconic brand with nearly 80 years of defining Western style, has teamed up with Nashville-based imogene + willie to create a collaborative collection rooted in authentic domestic craftsmanship. Rather than simply slapped-on logos, the Nashville crew was given keys to Wrangler's rich archives, unlocking original patterns, vintage visual assets, and rare fabrics. The result is a thoughtful blend of heritage design and modern, US-made construction that honors the workers, mills, and legacy behind classic Americana denim.The first drop is anchored by deadstock, rigid selvedge denim sourced directly from the legendary Cone Mills White Oak Mill. Highlights include a faithful reproduction of the rare 1964 10MW jean—which Wrangler only produced for a single year—alongside the 10WW, a tailored adaptation featuring a higher rise and fitted waist designed for a flattering feminine fit. Rounding out the first release is a limited-edition Studio Tee inspired by 90s-era all-over graphic prints featuring custom Western artwork.October 24 brings Drop 2, shifting focus toward rugged broken twill denim and woven fabrics developed in partnership with Mount Vernon Mills, the last remaining large-scale denim mill in the US. Cowboy lovers can look forward to the iconic 1950s "Cowboy Cut" 13MWZ jean and its feminine counterpart, the 14MWZ, available in washed indigo and black finishes with classic saddle-ready details like flat copper rivets and flat-felled inseams. The jacket selection shines with the zip-up 11MJZ denim jacket and the 12MJZ "championship" jacket—traditionally awarded to rodeo winners—recreated in overdyed, sunfaded cotton twill. Woven 27MW Western snap shirts, screen-printed graphic tees, and fleece crewnecks sewn directly in the USA complete the middle installment.The final rollout on November 7 delivers deadstock Cone Mills White Oak selvedge in unique colorways like black, brown, and…

a4977d3fa4:5b821dbb469f4594.title: JJJJound x New Balance 990v3 Revealed in Tan Suede
a4977d3fa4:5b821dbb469f4594.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5b821dbb469f4594.summary: SummaryThe FW26 JJJJound x New Balance 990v3 features a monolithic tan suede upper with contrasting black accents, dropping the previous mesh base.The USA-made shoe includes discreet branding, though an official release date and retail price have not yet been announced.For FW26, JJJJound and New Balance are delivering yet another variant of the New Balance 990v3, a silhouette the collaborators have reimagined time and time again since the very start of their partnership. The 990v3 is not only the first JJJJ x NB silhouette, debuting in 2018, but also the subject of four more releases since then. Now the JJJJound x New Balance 990v3 returns in a familiar palette, echoing the hues of their debut shoe with a streamlined executionComposed of full tan suede uppers, the design gets contrast from a black N logo on the lateral and an all-black sole. Across the tongue, “New Balance USA” calls out its USA-made provenance, having originated at the shoemaker’s New England production facilities. JJJJound’s signature branding appears only on the black insoles, aligning with the Montreal label's discreet approach to brand identity. Notably, the shoe borrows some details from the 2018 JJJJ x NB 990v3, including the tan suede upper details and the black N logo. However, for 2026, JJJJound forgoes the tonal detailing and mesh backdrop for a monolithic look, interrupted only by the few striking black details.As of the time of writing, JJJJound has not announced the official release date or retail price for its latest rendition of the New Balance 990v3. a4977d3fa4:7091c973912f4813.title: Bottega Veneta SS27 Is About Wearing Less & Feeling More
a4977d3fa4:7091c973912f4813.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7091c973912f4813.summary: SummaryLouise Trotter’s Bottega Veneta SS27 collection embraces relaxed tailoring, trading heavy furs for breathable layers, deconstructed coats, and translucent fabrics.Monochromatic everyday looks are elevated by delicate lace collars, scarf-fusions, and floral fringes, capturing a quiet, optimistic shift toward summer.On September 26th, Bottega Veneta presented its Spring/Summer 2027 collection at Milan Fashion Week, showcasing a more relaxed attitude in craft-forward details, intentional imperfection, and freedom — both physically and aesthetically. With her latest collection, Creative Director Louise Trotter distills the essence of “Summer beginning to bloom” through the lens of Bottega Veneta’s subtle but meticulous craftsmanship.Against the stiffer shoulders and busier looks of Trotter’s Spring/Summer 2026, the latest collection allows “definition” around gender and “tailoring” to “loosen,” in the words of the show notes. Relating her approach to the gentler seasons experienced in Milan, Trotter delivers “light changes” to the wardrobe for warmer months: leather outerwear remains, as do wool trousers and sharply cut blazers. However, gone are the ultra-plush fiberglass furs of Spring/Summer 2026, and the hairy overcoats from Fall/Winter 2026. This season features lighter layers, less strict silhouettes, and endearing details like florals, crochet, and translucent fabrics.One model wore a black trench coat with deconstructed sleeves and shoulders that freed the arms, while the collar of a black peacoat mutated into a light shoulder wrap on one side. There are also quite simple, everyday looks, with a poetic twist: a lived-in tan leather pant paired with a plain white long-sleeve top crowned by a lace collar, and white trousers were worn with a lustrous pearl-colored button-up that fused into a scarf hung around the neck. In the brand’s discreet style, most looks linger around monochromatic and black-and-white palettes, but a handful of numbers stood out in…

a4977d3fa4:e967e7e608fe2fc1.title: Willy Chavarria and adidas Originals Rework the Megaride for Fall 2026
a4977d3fa4:e967e7e608fe2fc1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:e967e7e608fe2fc1.summary: Name: Willy Chavarria x adidas Originals Mega Willy Low, Willy Chavarria x adidas Originals Willy Mega MidColorway: Black and Agave, BlackSKU: TBCMSRP: $230 USD, $280 USDRelease Date: October 3Where to Buy: adidas, CONFIRMED appadidas Originals and Willy Chavarria have built their Fall 2026 collection around the Megaride franchise, pairing the Mega Willy Low in Black and Agave with a Black Willy Mega Mid. The October capsule draws on '90s sportswear and scales up archival adidas shapes, continuing the designer's ongoing work with scale, identity and his own heritage.The footwear comes in two heights. The low-top Mega Willy Low arrives in two colorways, a Black pair and an Agave option, while the Willy Mega Mid raises the collar to a mid-cut and comes in Black only. Together the three pairs give the partnership's Megaride lineup both a sleek everyday profile and a higher-cut option.The apparel follows the same logic of scale. The sporting references stay recognizable, but they now sit inside a fashion-led silhouette that belongs as much to the street as to the track. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:a7aaccb56ff1f018.title: Tigris Li Taps Hankook Tire to Find the Quiet Moments in Her Creative Process
a4977d3fa4:a7aaccb56ff1f018.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:a7aaccb56ff1f018.summary: Artist and technologist Tigris Li is pushing the boundaries of creativity. Through her new AI-powered fragrance experience, Index, she envisions sensory impulses with electronic hardware to encourage play. Though the output hinges on interaction and conversation, the practice behind making the installations is a quiet one, requiring her to pay close attention to engineering. In a new installment of Day in the Life, Li lets Hypebeast in on this creative process, which takes place across London. Going from her new studio to several stores and workshops around the city, the feature follows her in the driver’s seat of the electric-powered BMW iX3, equipped with Hankook’s revolutionary iON Evo tires, which make the journey smooth and help her maintain an element of peace between stops. “My creative process isn’t in just one location,” the technologist shares from the confines of her new studio space where she begins her day. “It can start wherever I am, whether that’s on a drive, on a walk, or at home. It’s a constant thing.” As routine dictates, she flicks through her handy red sketchbooks, reviews the daily tasks, and sets off in the SUV ready to pick up the final components for her installation. After weaving through traffic, Li selects the materials she needs from her go-to workshop and heads to the next destination to pick up the new laser-cut pieces making up the furniture element. “Days like today can be chaotic, but as soon as I get in the car, the noise of the city fades away; it really lets me tune in,” she mentions on the journey. The technologist particularly admires the addition of the iON Evo tires to her journey, sharing that the noise reduction “lets you put your thoughts together while still being with the movement of the city.”Once the components are collected, it's back to the studio to assemble the installation with Index co-founder Isabella Smith. “We’re excited to bring this to the public with our launch, she says. Just like Hankook’s tires have…

a4977d3fa4:9438c6106b8f3e65.title: Louis Vuitton’s Monterey Timepiece Returns in Glossy Black and Heritage Green
a4977d3fa4:9438c6106b8f3e65.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:9438c6106b8f3e65.summary: Summary Louis Vuitton expands the Monterey with new black and green ceramic models.Both retain the 37mm pebble-shaped case and 12 o’clock crown.An in-house automatic movement replaces the original 1988 quartz caliber. Louis Vuitton is bringing the Monterey into its permanent collection with two new ceramic interpretations that revisit the House’s earliest experiments in wristwatch design. The Monterey traces back to the LV I and LV II, created in 1988 with Italian architect and designer Gae Aulenti as Louis Vuitton’s first wristwatches. Defined by their pebble-shaped cases and unconventional crown placement at 12 o’clock, the originals have attracted renewed collector interest in recent years, appearing in Nicolas Ghesquière’s FW25 and SS26 presentations as watches, pendants and belt accessories.Following the 2025 revival of the Monterey in a 188-piece yellow-gold edition, Louis Vuitton now translates the design into glossy black and green ceramic, bringing both versions into the collection on a non-limited basis. Both models retain the original’s compact 37mm proportions and recognizable Clous de Paris steel crown at 12 o’clock, while introducing a more contemporary material treatment. The green edition takes a near-monochromatic approach, matching its polished ceramic case with a matte green lacquer dial, white railway track and vivid yellow lacquered hour and minute hands — a color choice that nods to the yellow stitching associated with Louis Vuitton leather goods.The black version creates a sharper contrast between its glossy black ceramic case and matte white lacquer dial, punctuated by red hands and railway markings and a fine blue seconds hand; its black grained calfskin strap continues the red detailing through contrast stitching. Louis Vuitton produces the ceramic cases from zirconium oxide and pigments before machining, firing them above 1,000°C, manually grinding and finally hand-polishing them to achieve the Monterey’s smooth, reflective pebble-like…

a4977d3fa4:1b94da6f2c518ce4.title: Burton Raids Zeb Powell's Wardrobe for "Zeb's Closet," a Baggy Outerwear Collection
a4977d3fa4:1b94da6f2c518ce4.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:1b94da6f2c518ce4.summary: Summary Burton's first globally available outerwear and apparel collection with Zeb Powell pairs waterproof shells and utility details with his signature oversized fitsThe lineup spans heavyweight hoodies, jerseys, rugby shirts, shorts, reversible bucket hats and a reversible insulated vest designed for layeringA traveling installation called Zeb's Mobile Closet debuts in New York City before visiting key snowboarding destinations around the world Burton has launched Zeb's Closet, an outerwear and apparel collection built in partnership with team rider Zeb Powell. Burton bills it as the first globally available collection it has created with the snowboarder. The range is designed around Powell's personal style rather than performance specs alone, combining technical outerwear with the loose, oversized pieces he wears both on the mountain and off it.The design brief was simple: build what Powell would actually wear. In practice, that means waterproof outerwear, utility-driven detailing and premium construction, all cut into the roomy, baggy silhouettes closely tied to his look. Every piece is meant to allow unrestricted movement, so the fit supports the loose, freestyle way he rides.The rest of the range pushes further into streetwear. Heavyweight hoodies, jerseys, rugby shirts, tees, shorts and pants sit alongside reversible bucket hats and technical shells. All of it is intended to be stacked in layers and worn long after the last lap of the day. The standout piece is a reversible insulated vest, which gives riders a functional mid-layer with enough personality to wear on its own."It's called Zeb's Closet because it's actually what I would wear - on the mountain and off the mountain," Powell said in a statement. That on-and-off-hill crossover fits the larger picture Burton sees in the collection. The brand views Powell as the face of a new generation of snowboarding shaped by creativity, self-expression and the communities changing what the sport looks like. "Zeb…

d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.title: The Scramble for the Open Seas
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.author: Michael Albertus
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.summary: Over the last half millennium, societies around the globe competed to divide up the world’s land. Nearly every square inch of soil outside Antarctica is now owned and tucked within national borders. But the oceans have largely been spared that fate. There were times throughout history when countries tried to gate and regulate the seas, but they were too vast to be controlled for long periods. During the Cold War, as technology made it far easier to imagine partitioning the world’s waterways and seabeds, great powers avoided an unrestrained race to grab the oceans. Most governments agreed to deal with them through a patchwork of treaties and multilateral bodies that sought to guarantee freedom of navigation in international waters and assign coastal seabeds to adjacent littoral states.

d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.title: The Trouble With the Nuclear-AI Analogy
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.author: Christopher LaRoche, Ankit Panda
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.summary: In humanity’s quest to constrain the dangers from fast-advancing artificial intelligence, many have looked to the most revolutionary technology that preceded it: nuclear weapons. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has called artificial intelligence “far more dangerous than nukes.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who assigns The Making of the Atomic Bomb to employees and has likened himself to the Manhattan Project scientist Leo Szilard, describes the most powerful AI models as “weaponizable nuclear materials.” When asked how a technology such as AI can be regulated, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman often references the world’s nuclear materials watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency. Even the director of the CIA, John Ratcliffe, has made the same comparison.These comparisons capture real parallels. Like nuclear weapons, frontier AI is powerful and hard to control. Like nuclear technology, it can be used for good or for ill. And like the Cold War arms race, the race for AI breakthroughs may reorder the global balance of power. The nuclear analogy, then, seems to offer a blueprint for how to effectively govern a promising but potentially dangerous technology such as AI.

fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.title: What Does Venture Capital Actually Finance ? Scale and Structure around the World
fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.author: Mauro, Paolo
fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.summary: Venture capital is widely viewed as financing knowledge-intensive, R&D-driven startups, but owing to data constraints, this view has been based largely on high-income economies. By taking a global perspective, this paper documents that what venture capital finances differs systematically across economies, varying with institutional and business conditions rather than following a single model. Using a new cross-country dataset that harmonizes firm-level venture capital records with equity issuance data for more than 150 economies, the data shows that VC markets differ across countries not only in scale but in kind. Outside high-income countries, rather than being concentrated in knowledge intangibles, venture capital tilts–at both the sector and firm levels–toward organizational intangibles such as distribution, logistics, and payments. Highlighting the unique features of venture capital, this pattern is absent from public equity markets, where sectoral composition is far more similar across income levels. An accounting decomposition separates venture capital depth into the rate at which firms enter the market and the funding each entrant attracts, and entry accounts for the largest cross-country gaps. Moreover, the business environment is associated with VC primarily through entry, linked both to the size of the market and to the composition of what venture capital finances, the latter through entry into knowledge-intensive sectors in particular.

fc066e842d:1ada7049cb8f2e03.title: Standardizing Business Process Documentation for Operational Transition: A Case Study of Employee Administration Data Entry at PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Persero) Tbk
fc066e842d:1ada7049cb8f2e03.author: Athira, Celia
fc066e842d:1ada7049cb8f2e03.summary: Organizational transitions that transfer operational activities from internal units to external partners depend heavily on the availability of standardized process documentation. This study examines the business process of Employee Administration (EA) Kedinasan data entry within the Employee & Organization Data Operation (EODO) unit of PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, undertaken as part of the company's preparation to transfer data-entry activities to an external partner, PT Infomedia Nusantara. Using a descriptive-qualitative case study approach grounded in Business Process Management (BPM) theory, the study maps the existing (as-is) process through direct observation, documentation review, and discussion with field supervisors, and evaluates it using SWOT analysis to identify internal and external factors shaping the transition. The findings show that although the EA Kedinasan process already possesses a structured workflow supported by verification and approval checkpoints and a centralized SAP-based system, its documentation remains fragmented across multiple work instructions and lacks an integrated reference that can function effectively as a knowledge-transfer medium for an external partner. The study recommends the consolidation of Business Process diagrams, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Work Instructions, and a Playbook into a single coherent documentation package, which was implemented in part during the internship. Beyond its immediate organizational relevance, the case illustrates a broader tension in business process transitions: technically sound processes can still generate transition risk when explicit-knowledge artifacts are not consolidated for an external audience. The study contributes a practitioner-grounded account of how BPM and knowledge-transfer principles operate in a real outsourcing transition within a large Indonesian state-owned enterprise, and offers implications for organizations preparing similar administrative…

fc066e842d:f89f05c8bc834f39.title: Reversibility as a Factor of Production: A General Theory of the Economics of Error
fc066e842d:f89f05c8bc834f39.author: YAHYA, Ould Amar
fc066e842d:f89f05c8bc834f39.summary: What the Article proposes. All growth is born of trials — projects launched, firms founded, techniques attempted — and most trials fail. What each society does with those failures is, this Article argues, the most decisive and least measured variable in economics. Where honest failure leaves its author with his capabilities, his assets and his reputation, people try often, learn fast and prosper; where failure destroys — perpetual debt, stigma, disqualification, personal ruin — the most rational agents stop trying, and the economy dies out for want of experiments. The Article gives this intuition a complete theoretical body: it introduces the “reversibility coefficient ρ, ” the fraction of his capabilities an agent retains after an honest failure, elevates it to a factor of production on a par with capital and labor, and endows it with a law of formation, a geometry, theorems and an instrument of measurement. A pharmaceutical laboratory screens ten thousand molecules to retain a single one for a drug; the 9, 999 failures are not losses but precious information — each closes a path, sharpens the map and brings the medicine closer, to the point that laboratories parse their competitors’ failures line by line. The Article asks that the economy as a whole treat error as the laboratory treats it — a raw material of discovery — and not as a punitive society treats it, where a mistake closes the future to whoever makes it. The thesis holds that development begins neither with savings nor with capital goods, but when falling ceases to mean being destroyed. Why reversibility truly is a factor of production. Economic science admits as a factor of production any magnitude that meets three criteria: it is scarce and costly to produce; its increase raises output, other factors held constant; and it accumulates and depreciates like a stock. Reversibility passes all three tests. It is productive: with capital, labor and talent held identical, ρ governs both the number of trials…

fc066e842d:dea68a113565c652.title: Towards a dynamic conceptualisation of the Regional Innovation System: The Systemic Knowledge Network Continuum
fc066e842d:dea68a113565c652.author: Nick Clifton
fc066e842d:dea68a113565c652.summary: The Regional Innovation Systems (RIS) framework explains regional innovation performance primarily through structural conditions and external knowledge flows. While this perspective has generated influential typologies and policy models, it offers limited insight into how RISs emerge and transform from within. This paper advances a dynamic perspective that conceptualises RIS development as a continuum from fragmented interaction to systemic integration. We argue that generative network mechanisms and systemic dimensions co-evolve recursively, enabling or constraining the formation of integrated RISs. By shifting attention from static structures to self-reinforcing dynamics, the framework provides a foundation for understanding RIS formation, transformation, and reversibility, and suggests a more adaptive, mechanism-oriented approach to policy.

fc066e842d:24d84e140192b3ce.title: Discovering Green: The Role of Organizational and Network Embeddedness in the Shift Toward Sustainability Research
fc066e842d:24d84e140192b3ce.author: Tom Broekel
fc066e842d:24d84e140192b3ce.summary: This study examines researchersâ€™ diversification into sustainability research, distinguishing between initial entry and subsequent engagement intensity. While the existing literature emphasises individual-level drivers, we argue that such diversification is also shaped by organisational and relational contexts. Using bibliometric data from the University of Stavanger, Norway, we show that network distance to sustainability-active colleagues is a key predictor: researchers who are structurally closer to engaged peers are more likely to enter the field and deepen their involvement. By contrast, department- and faculty-level sustainability activities show weaker, more context-dependent associations, with department-level effects disappearing once network variables are included. The findings highlight the importance of intra-organisational knowledge networks for sustainability-oriented research transitions.

5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.title: Presidential Address: Neighborhood Effects and Missing Markets for Opportunity
5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.author: info@aeaweb.org (Lawrence F. Katz1 1 Harvard University (email: lkatz@harvard.edu))
5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3197-3222 Abstract Experimental and quasi-experimental studies show that childhood neighborhoods have substantial causal impacts on children's adult earnings and other long-term socioeconomic outcomes. Several market failures are likely to lead to excessive residential segregation by parental income and to an undersupply of mixed-income neighborhoods. Missing markets for opportunity originate in capital market imperfections for borrowing on children's future earnings, neighbor spillovers, behavioral biases, and housing search frictions. Customized housing mobility services combined with subsidized housing vouchers can help low-income families move to higher-opportunity areas. Place-based policies that create mixed-income neighborhoods appear to increase long-term outcomes for less-advantaged children. (JEL I12, I32, I38, J13, J15, R23, R38)

5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.title: Contextually Private Mechanisms
5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.author: info@aeaweb.org (Andreas Haupt1 and Zoë Hitzig2 1 Stanford Digital Economy Lab (email: h4upt@stanford.edu) 2 Harvard Society of Fellows (email: zhitzig@g.harvard.edu))
5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3223-3262 Abstract A designer employs a dynamic protocol to elicit private information. Protocols produce a set of contextual privacy violations—information learned that may be superfluous given the context. A protocol is maximally contextually private if there is no protocol that produces a proper subset of the violations it produces, while implementing the choice rule. Contextual privacy violations arise when a choice rule makes some agents collectively, but not individually, pivotal. In auctions, designing for contextual privacy requires choosing an initial question posed to each agent and the order for querying agents. Ascending-join protocols are maximally contextually private for k-item Vickrey auctions. (JEL D44, D82)

5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.title: Manipulation-Robust Prediction
5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.author: info@aeaweb.org (Daniel Björkegren1, Joshua E. Blumenstock2 and Samsun Knight3 1 Columbia University (email: dan@bjorkegren.com) 2 UC Berkeley (email: jblumenstock@berkeley.edu) 3 University of…
5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3263-3293 Abstract An increasing number of decisions are guided by machine learning algorithms. But when consequential decisions are encoded in algorithms, individuals may strategically alter their behavior to achieve desired outcomes. This paper develops an empirical approach that adjusts decision algorithms to anticipate manipulation. By explicitly modeling incentives to manipulate, our approach produces decision rules that are stable under manipulation, even when the rules are fully transparent. We stress-test this approach through a large field experiment in Kenya. When implemented, linear strategy-robust decision rules outperform standard linear models such as LASSO. (JEL C45, C93, D12, D91, G51, O12, O16)

5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.title: Risk-Sharing Tests and Covariate Shocks: Drought, Floods, and Pests in Uganda
5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.author: info@aeaweb.org (Ethan Ligon1 1 University of California, Berkeley (email: ligon@berkeley.edu))
5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3294-3329 Abstract Efficient risk sharing implies a simple factor structure for marginal utilities of expenditure (MUEs): Pareto weights divided by a common price. The standard approach infers MUEs from total expenditures, implicitly assuming homothetic preferences, unitary income elasticities, and identical price elasticities. Risk-sharing tests using total expenditures work for idiosyncratic shocks (budgets change, but not prices), but not “covariate” shocks (prices change). I describe all preferences that permit one to infer MUEs from expenditures and estimate nonhomothetic MUEs to test whether covariate shocks are shared efficiently in Uganda. This delivers sensible results; the standard approach suggests that droughts, floods, and pests are beneficial. (JEL D12, D81, O12, O13, Q12)

5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.title: Optimal Public Transportation Networks: Evidence from the World's Largest Bus Rapid Transit System in Jakarta
5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.author: info@aeaweb.org (Gabriel Kreindler1, Arya Gaduh2, Tilman Graff3, Rema Hanna4 and Benjamin A. Olken5 1 Harvard University (email: gkreindler@g.harvard.edu) 2 University of Arkansas (email:…
5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3330-3379 Abstract Designing public transport networks involves trade-offs between coverage, service frequency, and direct service. We use the expansion of the bus system in Jakarta, Indonesia, to study these trade-offs. We analyze how new direct connections, changes in bus travel time, and wait-time reductions affect bus ridership and aggregate flows and estimate a transit network demand model by matching the route launch events. Commuters in Jakarta are 2–3 times more sensitive to wait time than bus time and inattentive to long routes. We develop a flexible framework to characterize optimal networks. A less concentrated network would increase ridership and commuter welfare. (JEL L92, L98, O18, R41, R42, R48)

5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.title: Corporate Tax Cuts, Firm Growth, and Workers' Earnings
5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.author: info@aeaweb.org (Patrick J. Kennedy1, Christine L. Dobridge2, Paul Landefeld3 and Jacob Mortenson4 1 UCLA, NBER, and JCT (email: pkennedy@econ.ucla.edu) 2 Federal Reserve Board (email:…
5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3380-3422 Abstract We study the effects of the largest corporate income tax cut in US history on firms and workers. To identify causal effects, we use employer-employee matched tax records and event studies comparing similarly sized firms in the same industry that faced divergent tax changes due to their preexisting legal status. Tax cuts cause increases in firms' investment, sales, profits, employment, and payrolls, with earnings gains concentrated among highly paid workers. In the short run, 87 percent of private income gains flow to the top 10 percent of the income distribution. (JEL D22, D31, G31, H25, H32, J23, L25)

5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.title: Marriage, Fertility, and Cultural Integration in Italy
5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.author: info@aeaweb.org (Alberto Bisin1 and Giulia Tura2 1 New York University (email: alberto.bisin@nyu.edu) 2 LUISS University (email: gtura@luiss.it))
5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3423-3463 Abstract We study cultural integration as an equilibrium outcome of marital matching along cultural and education lines and intrahousehold investment decisions regarding fertility and cultural socialization. Our model allows us to identify cultural-ethnic-group-specific investment parameters and spousal preferences for marital matching. Structural estimates reveal a strong demand to preserve cultural identity on the part of immigrants and limited acceptance of the immigrants' cultural diversity on the part of natives. Furthermore, these estimates reveal a substantial heterogeneity of the parental value of children's education across cultures. Nonetheless, our estimates simulate substantial—though heterogeneous—cultural integration rates across immigrant groups. (JEL D13, J12, J13, J15, Z13)

5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.title: Defying Distance? The Provision of Medical Services in the Digital Age
5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.author: info@aeaweb.org (Amanda Dahlstrand1 1 University of Zurich (email: amanda.dahlstrand@econ.uzh.ch))
5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3464-3509 Abstract Digital platforms reduce geographic frictions, enabling better matching between service providers and users. I quantify reallocation gains in Swedish online health care, using nationwide time-conditional random assignment between patients and physicians. Matching high-risk patients with doctors effective at reducing Emergency Room visits lowers such visits by 4.4 percent (SE 1.3); reallocations also reduce Counter-Guideline antibiotics by 3.1 percent (1.4). I find limited trade-offs in matching; horizontal differentiation among doctors and varied patient needs allow improvement in multiple outcomes simultaneously. Efficiency-enhancing reallocations also affect equity. The findings highlight the potential for care reorganization aligning provider heterogeneity with patient needs when geographic constraints are lifted. (JEL C78, H51, I11, I13, I14, I18)

5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.title: The Environmental Bias of Corporate Income Taxation
5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.author: info@aeaweb.org (Luigi Iovino1, Thorsten Martin2 and Julien Sauvagnat3 1 Bocconi University (email: luigi.iovino@unibocconi.it) 2 Frankfurt School of Finance and Management (email: t.martin@fs.de) 3…
5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3510-3551 Abstract We study the relationship between corporate income taxation and carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in the United States. We show CO2-intensive firms benefit more from the tax advantage of debt and pay lower income taxes on their capital income. Building on these new facts, we provide evidence that a cut in the corporate income tax rate leads to a larger expansion of clean firms. We develop a multisector general equilibrium model that accounts for our evidence and quantify the impact of corporate tax reforms on aggregate emissions. A policy that eliminates the tax advantage of debt could reduce aggregate emissions without affecting GDP. (JEL D22, G32, H25, H32, Q52, Q54, Q58)

5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.title: Rationing by Race
5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.author: info@aeaweb.org (Manasvini Singh1 and Atheendar Venkataramani2 1 Carnegie Mellon University and NBER (email: msingh01@cmu.edu) 2 University of Pennsylvania and NBER (email:…
5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3552-3585 Abstract We document how deepening resource scarcity results in rationing on the basis of race in a high-stakes setting: health care. Using detailed, time stamped data on 107,000 inpatient admissions to a large health system, we find that in-hospital mortality increases for Black but not White patients as hospitals reach capacity. These findings are not explained by differential patient selection. We identify rationing by wait times as a mechanism, documenting that sicker Black patients wait longer for care than healthier White patients at almost all capacity levels. Text analysis of unstructured clinical notes reveals rationing of provider effort as another mechanism. (JEL I11, I12, I14, J15)

5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.title: Intergenerational Impacts of Secondary Education: Experimental Evidence from Ghana
5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.author: info@aeaweb.org (Esther Duflo1, Pascaline Dupas2, Elizabeth Spelke3 and Mark Walsh4 1 MIT and Collège de France (email: eduflo@mit.edu) 2 Princeton University (email: pdupas@princeton.edu) 3 Harvard…
5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3586-3621 Abstract We provide experimental evidence on the intergenerational impacts of secondary education subsidies in a low-income context, leveraging a randomized controlled trial and 15-year longitudinal follow-up. Secondary school scholarships delay fertility, reduce unwanted pregnancies, and change partner selection. Under-one mortality is reduced by half. We also document cognitive development gains of 0.24 standard deviations of test scores by age five among children of female scholarship recipients. Means-tested secondary school scholarships are a high-return investment, with a conservatively estimated US$4.1 in benefits for each US$1 the policy would cost the government in the long run. (JEL H52, I12, I21, I26, J13, J16, O15)

21113a7a19:03152dfb5a3bd529.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:03152dfb5a3bd529.summary: Here's the announcement of a new prize, initially to be awarded for work in the social sciences, reflecting the fact that social science can be politically contentious. The Carob Trust Prize for Academic Courage : Celebrating the Pursuit of Knowledge "The Carob Trust Prize honors academics who pursue bold ideas that challenge prevailing orthodoxies—whether political, intellectual, or methodological—and hold the potential to reshape knowledge, policy, or society. The Prize supports scholars whose work is original, rigorous, impactful, and courageous—even when it is unpopular. " "Selection Criteria Intellectual Independence : A proven commitment to following logic and evidence wherever they lead, regardless of academic or political pressure. Non-Conformist Ideas : Originality and boldness of research agenda. Willingness to ask questions that others avoid—whether uncomfortable, underfunded, or unfashionable. Impact and Vindication : Work of excellent quality that has shifted academic debate, public discourse, or policy. Evidence that ideas criticized at the time have proven—through data, replication, or influence—to possess enduring value. " "Timeline Nov. 1, 2026: Nominations due Spring 2027:Announcement of Prize winners " ####### Here's a column in the WSJ about the prize: An Award for Scholars Who Tell the Truth The Carob Trust Prize for Academic Courage will honor social scientists who face unjustified attacks.
